# Platform Build Log

Append-only log of work sessions. Each session adds exactly one row, in two edits:

1. **At session start** (before any real work): append a row with status `⏳ IN FLIGHT — {step name}`, commit it immediately as its own standalone commit.
2. **At session end** (after the real work is done, tested, and typechecked): update that same row to `✅ DONE — {step name}`, filling in the real commit hash of the work, then commit the update (either folded into the final commit or immediately after it).

If a session dies, crashes, or is abandoned mid-way, its row stays `⏳ IN FLIGHT`, which is itself the record that an attempt was made and didn't finish.

See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for the exact instructions.

| 2026-07-28 | ✅ DONE | PlatformAdmin AI Billing page + live StatusBar segments — Phase 3 of the AI Cost Governance & Billing Rollup (#51), surfacing the `ai_usage_events` rows Phase 1 (#49) guaranteed get written and Phase 2 (#50) expanded for traceability. **REUSED EXISTING INFRA THROUGHOUT, no parallel mechanisms:** the `ai-cost` SSE channel rides the existing generic `sse-hub.ts` (no new transport), the client uses the existing `useLiveStream.ts` EventSource hook (no second EventSource implementation), the popover is the existing `components/ui/hover-card.tsx` primitive, the delta chip borrows the existing `.count-pop` / `.sale-flash-exit` animations rather than adding a third, and the page registration follows Active Directory Phase 1 (`70a255ba`) line-for-line. **BACKEND:** new `admin-ai-billing.ts` (`requireAdmin`, `logger.child({ channel: "engine.ai-cost-governance" })`) with `GET /admin/ai-billing/events` (filterable on mspId/customerId/from/to/nodeType/feature/costOwner/generatedArtifactType, paginated, full Phase-2 traceability projection), `GET /admin/ai-billing/summary?range=today\|month` (total + by-cost-owner/by-MSP/by-feature) and `GET /admin/ai-billing/recent?limit=N`. Pure date-boundary and rollup logic split into `ai-billing-rollup.ts` so it is unit-testable without an express+drizzle mock harness. **DESIGN DECISIONS THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING:** (1) **Seed + delta, never replay-as-total.** `broadcastToHubWithReplay` caches only the LAST event per channel, which here is a single per-call DELTA, not a running total — so the client seeds both totals from `/summary` on mount and adds SSE frames on top. The live-stream route must keep NOT enabling replay for channel-firehose subscribers (it doesn't today) or a delta would be counted twice on every reconnect; this is recorded in the `AI_COST_SSE_CHANNEL` docblock so nobody enables it later without thinking. The client-side guard is a last-applied-frame-id marker, so a re-render never re-adds a counted cost and a reconnect (which empties `useLiveStream`'s buffer) still applies only genuinely new frames. (2) **The broadcast is passive by construction.** It sits in its OWN `try/catch` immediately after the insert succeeds, so a hub fault can neither skip the MSP ledger debit below it nor make `recordAiUsage` reject (usage recording is documented non-fatal) — and a FAILED insert broadcasts nothing, so money never appears on the status bar that no ledger query can account for. Both are asserted as explicit negative tests, not assumed. `.returning()` gained `occurredAt` so the frame carries the row's real timestamp rather than the moment of the broadcast. (3) **Viewer-local day boundaries.** `/summary` takes a `tzOffsetMinutes` param (the browser's own `getTimezoneOffset()`) so "Today" rolls over at the admin's midnight, not UTC's — a US-based admin would otherwise watch the segment reset at 8pm. Documented limitation: the offset is treated as FIXED across the range, so a month straddling a DST transition is off by an hour at one edge; stated in `resolveRangeBounds`, not hidden. (4) **DEVIATION FROM THE ISSUE, deliberate:** the spec sketched a `▲ $0.0034` delta chip, but `ai_usage_events.cost_cents` is an INTEGER column and `computeTokenCostCents` uses `Math.ceil`, so a single call is never finer-grained than $0.01 — rendering four decimals would imply a precision the ledger does not carry. Deltas display as `$X.XX`. **FRONTEND:** `AiBillingPage.tsx` at `/system/ai-billing` (summary cards, URL-backed filters following the `RunHistoryPage` convention so the StatusBar click-through deep-links and stays shareable, expandable per-row detail showing every traceability column). Two StatusBar segments built from the same `Led` + `count-pop` pieces `liveVisitors` already uses; `useAiCostSegments` owns seed-then-delta plus the chip lifecycle and is threaded down from `GlobalIDEShell` as a prop, so `StatusBar` stays presentational exactly like `liveVisitors`/`campaignBadges` and never fetches for itself. Rapid successive calls accumulate into ONE chip with its timers cleared and restarted, so nothing stacks or leaks. An unseeded total stays `null` and its segment hides rather than rendering a `$0.00` nobody verified. **ALSO:** `engine.ai-cost-governance` added to `admin-live-stream.ts`'s `CHANNEL_TAXONOMY` — Phase 1 introduced that logger channel but never listed it in the picker. **VERIFIED:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in admin-panel; api-server clean apart from 6 pre-existing `vi.fn`-typing errors in `ai-usage-sink.test.ts`, **proven pre-existing by re-running tsc with every one of this task's changes removed and getting the byte-identical 6 errors** — not assumed from the fact that the file wasn't touched. 54 new tests (27 route/helper, 11 broadcast, 16 hook, 16 StatusBar), the two api-server files registered in `vitest.config.ts`'s hardcoded include list. ROOT CAUSE (traced, not assumed): Graph checks that fail because the tenant lacks a SKU were conflated with two unrelated states. A 401 `Unauthorized — Account is not provisioned` hit `graphFetchForTenant`'s blanket "any 401 → consent revoked" path → `markTenantConsentRevoked()` bulk-flipped EVERY `tenant_monitor_profiles` row for the tenant to `consent_revoked` (a tenant-wide contamination from one unprovisioned feature) + threw `ConsentRevokedError` (which then short-circuited all remaining checks); a 403 `Authentication_RequestFromNonPremiumTenantOrB2CTenant` fell through `isConsentErrorBody` and surfaced as a generic `error`. Either way `pkgResult.runStatus` became `consent_revoked`/`partial_failure`, so `diagnostics-runner`'s `finalStatus` never reached `"completed"` — and the seeded Assessment Document Generation workflow's `assessment_doc_gate` requires `msp_diagnostic_runs.status = 'completed'`, so a license-gapped tenant could NEVER get documents generated. FIX (D1) `graph.ts`: new `classifyGraphError()` + `LicenseGapError`; `graphFetchForTenant` now reads the 401/400/403 body and, on a documented AAD premium error CODE (`Authentication_RequestFromNonPremiumTenantOrB2CTenant`/`RequestFromNonPremiumTenantOrB2CTenant`) or the stable `"not provisioned"` / `"doesn't have premium license"` phrases, throws `LicenseGapError` with a customer-safe feature name and does NOT flip consent — genuine consent errors (`invalid_grant`/`AADSTS65001`/`consent_required`/`InvalidAuthenticationToken`, and any other bare 401) still auto-revoke exactly as before; only these exact structural signals are reclassified (no fragile heuristic, per the no-silent-reclassification rule). (D2) `monitor-executor.ts`: new `"license_gap"` `CheckResult` status — license gaps no longer set the consent short-circuit (each check may need a different SKU, so all checks now run), and the run-status computation treats them as neither error nor consent_revoked, so a tenant whose only non-ok results are license gaps reaches `"completed"` HONESTLY, unblocking the doc gate WITHOUT weakening the gate's own `= 'completed'` check (fixed upstream, per non-goal). Adds `licenseGapCount`/`licenseGapFeatures` to `PackageRunResult` + `licenseGap` to the engine breakdown, and stamps definitive falsy license flags (`hasAADP1orP2:false`/`hasDefender:false` — the same keys the M365 script parser writes) into the license_gap profile row so the existing signal engine can derive an upsell signal off a Graph-only scan. `diagnostics-runner.ts`: license_gap findings are `info` (never critical/red), counted in the new `checks_license_gap` column + run `summary.licenseGapFeatures`, named in the HTML report's summary; `finalStatus` now reaches `completed` via the upstream fix (unchanged mapping). (D3) `portal-assessment.ts` exposes `checksLicenseGap` + `licenseGapFeatures` from the run/summary; `AssessmentWizard.tsx` scan-complete copy now reads e.g. "9 checks passed. Now writing up your findings… N checks couldn't run because your tenant doesn't have Microsoft Entra ID Premium (P1/P2) or Microsoft Defender for Office 365 — that's a licensing gap, not a security issue." and scores the ring over EVALUABLE checks (ok+error, excluding license gaps) so a fully-passing-but-unlicensed tenant reads green, not "31% red". | 2026-07-21 | ✅ DONE | Fix Typewriter Headline Randomization + Repeat Bug — confirmed root cause of both bugs by tracing `useHeroHeadlines.ts` + the seed SQL: `FALLBACK_HEADLINE`'s text is byte-identical to the DB's `sort_order = 0` row (`2026-07-19-hero-headlines.sql`), and the hook seeded `headlines` state to `[FALLBACK_HEADLINE]` (array length 1) before the `/api/public/hero-headlines` fetch resolved. Since `headlineIndex % headlines.length` is always `0 % 1 = 0`, the rotation was trapped on that single entry — typing, pausing, and deleting it in a full loop, potentially more than once — for however long the fetch took; because that entry's text is identical to the real first headline, this was visually indistinguishable from "the first headline plays twice" before the real rotation ever started. Separately, `public-hero.ts` always returned rows `orderBy(asc(sortOrder))` and nothing on the client ever reordered them, so rotation order was always fixed DB order. FIX: added a `loaded` flag set once the fetch settles (success, empty, or failure); while unloaded and still on the 1-element fallback array, the typing effect now holds at the fully-typed fallback instead of deleting/retyping it in a loop. On successful fetch, the headline set is now shuffled once (Fisher-Yates) before being stored, and `headlineIndex`/`charCount`/`phase` are reset so the real rotation starts clean at a random order — not re-shuffled on every cycle, only once per page load. Only `useHeroHeadlines.ts` touched — `Home.tsx`, the admin Hero Headlines management screen, and headline content untouched, per task scope. `shane-mccaw-consulting` typechecks clean (`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, exit 0). Only `AssessmentOffer` carries `isFree` to the storefront (`MonitoringTier` has NO isFree field at all — proven in `useCatalog.ts`, so a true monitoring_tier can never free-route; Shane's "monitoring package" is catalog serviceType=`assessment`, the tenant-scan product), so `tierToService` set `service.isFree=true`, the checkout button routed to `handleFreeCheckout` → `POST /api/portal/checkout/free` (NO Stripe), and `provisionFreeOnboarding` provisioned the account + session + tenant scan + confirmation email for $0 — matching every observed symptom. The EXISTING server guard in `provisionFreeOnboarding` failed for the same reason: it summed `s.price ?? s.basePrice` (→ $0 for a price_cents-only row) so it did not reject. Confirmed the paid path had the identical gap in THREE more spots (create-session `missingPrices` + `rawPriceCents`, and the contract `computedFinalPrice` which only runs when `basePrice` is set). FIX (single root cause = legacy-only price reading; one commit `0f4c81ac`): (1) new `resolveServicePriceCents()` + `isServiceFree()` in `catalog-pricing.ts` as the single source of truth (price_cents first, then legacy price/base_price; free only when isFreeOffering OR zero across every field); (2) `/catalog/assessments` derives isFree via `isServiceFree` and surfaces the real retail price for display when legacy columns are null but price_cents is set (so a paid assessment shows "$250", not "$0"); (3) `provisionFreeOnboarding` (serves BOTH `/portal/checkout/free` and `/portal/onboarding/claim-free`) now rejects any service where `!isServiceFree(s)` with a warn log — the mandated hardened defensive guard, a second independent enforcement point behind the frontend routing that holds even if that routing is ever wrong again; (4) create-session `missingPrices` + `rawPriceCents` now honor `price_cents` as a fallback so the paid path charges the real amount instead of erroring "no price configured"/charging $0. Verified correct across all four data states (price_cents-only paid, legacy paid, genuinely free, isFreeOffering promo) — the free assessment funnel stays free, only genuinely-priced items flip to Stripe. Both are recorded here because the wrong intermediate conclusion is the useful part of the record. **Cost Engine — initial (partly wrong) diagnosis:** the chain looked like it broke purely on a check KEY. `sku_price_reference` really does hold `ENTERPRISEPACK` at 2300 cents, and all three consumers — `portal-assessment.ts`'s `stats.licenseWasteMonthlyCents`/`stats.licenseWaste`, the `licensing.wasteEstimateBreakdown` metric that actually drives /m365-health's Cost Efficiency panel, and `cio-narrative-generator.ts` — hardcoded `cost:license-waste-estimate`, the only `cost:*` key referenced anywhere in code or SQL. `8b6e8ea2` therefore resolved the waste check at query time, scoring candidate `{label: count}` maps by how many keys matched `sku_price_reference`. **Why that was wrong, from live data (PART A, customer 4):** `cost:license-waste-estimate` DOES NOT EXIST in `monitor_checks`; the seven real cost checks are duplicate-assignments (`/users`, countDuplicates), entra-license-tier-distribution / license-count-by-sku / utilization-by-sku (all `/subscribedSkus`, groupByCount(skuPartNumber)), group-based-licensing-adoption (`/groups`), underutilized-premium (`/users`), and unused-unassigned-licenses (`/subscribedSkus`, count(consumedUnits)). NONE emits a per-SKU wasted-SEAT count, and two are active traps: (a) `cost:unused-unassigned-licenses` is MISNAMED relative to its mapping — `count` counts items whose field is non-null, and every subscribed SKU has a `consumedUnits`, so the observed `unusedLicenseCount: 4` means "this tenant subscribes to 4 SKUs", not "4 wasted seats", and it goes UP when the tenant buys a product; (b) every `groupByCount(skuPartNumber)` over `/subscribedSkus` returns ONE ROW PER SKU, which is exactly why the observed breakdown read `ENTERPRISEPACK: 1` — not one wasted seat. Those maps are SKU-keyed and numeric, so `8b6e8ea2`'s scoring fallback would have selected one and priced `1 × $23.00 = $23/month` of waste that does not exist. A real-looking fabricated figure is strictly worse than the null it replaced. **The real fix (`6bcd3273`):** `license-waste-source.ts` no longer infers waste from ANY `extractedProperties` count map (`extractCountMaps` + price-catalog scoring deleted). It computes the figure where it genuinely lives — the stored `/subscribedSkus` Graph page, in which each SKU carries `prepaidUnits.enabled` (bought) and `consumedUnits` (assigned): unused = enabled − consumed, floored at 0, which is arithmetically defined rather than name-inferred. Candidates are selected by ENDPOINT (`%subscribedskus%`), not key name, precisely because this catalog's key names have proven unreliable. Honesty guards, each returning null rather than a plausible number: a page carrying `@odata.nextLink` is REFUSED outright (only page 1 is persisted, so a truncated estate would silently underreport); a SKU missing either field is skipped rather than defaulted (a missing `consumedUnits` would otherwise read as "every seat wasted"); and a fully-assigned estate returns null so "no waste" renders as no waste rather than a $0 finding. `meta.seatLines`/`totalEnabledSeats` + `sourceCheckKey` expose the whole arithmetic, so no dollar figure is unattributed. **Risk Heat Map:** two genuinely different causes were flattened into one indistinguishable `no_data`. (1) A PHANTOM registry sourceKey — `identity.highRiskSigninCount` pointed at `identity:high-risk-signins`, which exists nowhere in the repo and which no migration ever created; the real catalog key is `identity:risky-signins`, curated into `core:security-baseline`. That cell could never resolve for any tenant. Registry corrected, and `resolveMonitorProfile` now returns `unknown_check_key` (not `no_data`) whenever a sourceKey has no `monitor_checks` row, so the whole bug class is visible in the API response instead of looking like an empty tenant. (2) Wrong VALUE on a populated cell — `checkNumericValue` took "the first numeric mapping targetField", then fell back to `_itemCount` (the raw Graph item count). For a stale-account check emitting both a directory-wide count and the stale count, that reported the entire directory under the "Stale Accounts" label. Replaced with `pickMappedValueField`, scoring targetFields by token overlap against the metric key leaf PLUS the check key leaf, falling back to first-numeric-wins only when nothing scores — a strict improvement with no behaviour change for the single-field mappings that are the common case. Every resolved scalar now carries `meta.valueSource` naming the exact field the number came from, and the same rule was applied to `monitorHistoryForTenant` so a sparkline point means what the headline value means. Frontend `resolvedEmptyReason` + `IntelligenceCore` tooltips/detail strip now distinguish "not wired to a real check yet" / "not in your scan package" / "no data collected". **Remaining sparseness is data, not code, and is now diagnosable:** only ~3 of the 26 heatmap metrics have sourceKeys inside the 29-check `core:security-baseline` curation — all 14 `drift:*` and the whole POLICIES family sit outside it by that migration's own explicit rationale. **Still open, handed to Shane:** `lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-07-26-cost-waste-and-heatmap-check-audit.sql` now records the confirmed Part A findings and adds A2/A3 — queries that compute the expected unused-seat count and dollar figure independently, straight from `raw_response`, so the UI can be compared against a number derived outside the code rather than merely believed. Parts B–D (phantom vs uncollected heatmap sourceKeys; whether `identity:stale-accounts`' mapping declares any numeric field or is still falling through to `_itemCount`) were truncated in the returned output and remain unanswered. New PART F documents the misnamed `cost:unused-unassigned-licenses` and queries where its wrong value is still consumed (its own `severity_rules`, plus `signal_derivation_rules`); NO correction is proposed for it, deliberately — `SUM(enabled − consumed)` is not expressible with any transform `monitor-executor.ts` implements, so making that check honest needs a new executor transform scoped as separate work, not a SQL edit swapping one wrong number for another. (2) `portal-assessment.ts`'s SOW rescope path now passes `forceRegenerate: true` explicitly; non-empty `selectedWorkstreamTitles` already suppresses reuse structurally, but the caller states the intent and it holds even when the requested list is empty. Result: `scanCheckResults` grows **1→137 monotonically for the entire run**, all 138 SSE messages arrive, `sseErr` 0, terminal detection fires on time, no cap and no dedup collapse (`executeMonitoringPackage` emits exactly one event per check over `orderedChecks`, so the `checkKey` dedup in scan-status-context never collapses two real checks). Under an instant server the panel already moved continuously (gauge 20→80 over 38 recomputes). **The real root cause is in `useRealTelemetryComparison.ts`, and it is that the hook had two silent, unrecoverable ways to DROP a recompute it had itself asked for.** (1) `load()`''s `if (inFlightRef.current) return;` discarded the request outright. Harmless for a mid-run tick — another check follows — but **fatal for the terminal recompute**, which is requested exactly ONCE (when `streamedRunId` goes null) milliseconds after the run''s last check, i.e. reliably *inside* the window of the recompute that last check just started, because the real `buildTelemetryComparison` (tenant profile build + signal rules + security engine + findings queries, ~a dozen queries, while the same DB services the scan) takes seconds. Dropped there it was never re-requested, so the panel kept a number computed partway through the run for good. (2) `if (!res.ok) return;` discarded a failed response with no retry, and since the call is `{ silent: true }` there was no toast, no beacon and no console line — one failing window (the health engine timing out under the load of the very scan it measures is the obvious real candidate) froze the panel for the rest of the run *and past the end of it*, presenting a stale mid-run number under the settled "Health Engine" caption. **Both reproduced deterministically, then A/B''d against the same harness.** Cause 1: run ends at t=55.7s with a recompute in flight → **gauge frozen at 67, real final 92 never fetched, zero further requests in the following 34s**; with the fix the terminal recompute is queued behind the in-flight one and fires 2.8s later → **92**. One outstanding request (`want`), strongest reason wins (`terminal` > `live` > `initial`) so successive asks coalesce instead of piling up, and a single `pump()` decides when it may run — after the 4s throttle for a live tick, immediately for a terminal one, after exponential backoff (2/4/8/16/32s, 5 attempts) for a retry. `fetchWithAuth` is read through a ref, so a mid-run access-token refresh no longer rebuilds the whole recompute machinery and its effects. **The 4s cadence itself is deliberately unchanged** and its "flagged for Shane" note from #245 is preserved — #277 changed only what happens to a recompute the cadence asked for but could not perform. **Verification, at the bar the issue set**: a real full-length 137-check run (137s of checks) against a 6s-latency recompute — **23 distinct gauge values, 20 → 79, moving every ~6s with no stall anywhere across the entire run, gap bars moving in lockstep (-90%→-51% on the worst pillar), then the terminal jump to the real final 92** with the bars settling to -50/-38/-26/-14. 24 recomputes, 0 failures. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` at the exact pre-existing baseline (`SowScreen.tsx` TS7030 only), zero new errors; msp-portal `node --test` 52 pass / 0 fail. **Reported honestly, not fixed here**: a real silent SSE disconnect WAS observed once, mid-run at 135/137, and the stream never reconnects (`es.onerror = () => es.close()` in scan-status-context.tsx) — it did not freeze the panel, because the poll-driven terminal recompute still recovered it, and reconnection belongs in shell-wide scan-status code rather than in this panel-scoped fix. Confirmed from docs/signals.json (8 adoption-pillar signals; `licenseUtilizationPct` is an EXAMPLE row with confidence 0, so 7 real). **What the design gave and what was dropped.** previewDocumentBodies.ts's ADOPTION_READINESS was used for structure and tone only; most of its figures have no producer, and each drop is documented in pillarAdoption.ts's own header the way pillarSecurityPosture.ts documents its blastRadius / secureScoreTrend drops: Persona Readiness Analysis (no check produces a persona model or maps a user to a role — "Field Technician", "Bid Manager", "Legal Counsel" are already on FIXTURE_LEAKS); Workflow Alignment Assessment (the only `workflow:*` signal in the catalog, `hasManualProcessOverhead`, is an example row seeded for the rule builder with confidence 0 and every impact 0); Training & Enablement Gaps (no training record, no department roster); the PROJECTED SCORE and the point attribution ("enablement alone moves Adoption from 46 to an estimated 61", "Adoption contributes 22 points of available gain") — the other six state neither and COPILOT_IMPACT_RULES forbids both in prompt form, so introducing one here would have made this the only report promising a customer a number it cannot owe them; the drift claims; Self-Resolution Actions (#343 precedent — remediation is the guide's job); and all three figures, including `usageTrend`, whose real-looking candidate (`pillar-trend.ts`'s #356 series) is the ADOPTION PILLAR SCORE over time and not usage over time. **TREND_DIRECTION_GAP is the point specific to this report and it came out of reading the real endpoints**: three checks carry the word "trend" in their catalogue labels while every one of them reads `period='D7'` — a single seven-day window, collected once, with no earlier window persisted to diff against. So "usage has been flat for two periods" and "412 users have not opened Teams in 30 days" are not merely unbacked but unbackable from these checks. The report says so to the reader; the prompts forbid the claim; the two cannot contradict each other. All three declared gaps render unconditionally, name no check key (#441) and carry no digit, each asserted by the suite. **Pending SQL for Shane:** `document_types` has no `adoption_report` row (2026-08-06-document-generation-ai-prompts.sql ROW 8 anticipated exactly this and says so), so `lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-08-document-types-adoption-report.sql` is written for him to run. Nothing breaks unrun — `liveDocumentFor` matches docType OR the design's exact title. Its catalogue LABEL is deliberately "Copilot Adoption & Usage Report" and not the design's "Workflow Readiness", which would promise in the admin UI a measurement the report itself refuses to make.
